headline: Russia says its defenses intercepted over 1,300 Ukrainian drones in a major attack
briefing: Top stories right now: Russia says its defenses intercepted over 1,300 Ukrainian drones in a major attack; Trump backs return of ex-Nvidia boss after 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign launched; and Raye leads 2027 Grammy nominations as women dominate top categories.

keyDates.label: Carney–Xi meeting; Nvidia results; Ukraine arms meeting
keyDates.why: Carney meets Xi in Shenzhen (late Monday evening in Ontario), Ukraine's military backers meet at NATO headquarters in Brussels, Nvidia reports results after markets close, Israel's parliament votes on a new speaker and Iran's foreign minister visits Oman.

keyDates.label: APEC summit opens; Alaska ranked-choice count
keyDates.why: Leaders meet in Shenzhen on Nov. 18–19, and Alaska tabulates its Peltola–Sullivan Senate race if no one tops 50%.

keyDates.label: Trump meets Xi and Putin
keyDates.why: Trump holds a one-on-one with Xi and then a first-ever three-way meeting with Xi and Putin in Shenzhen, with nuclear weapons the stated focus.

keyDates.label: Senate Democrats vote; Stelco recall
keyDates.why: Democratic senators choose between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen for majority leader by secret ballot, and 175 laid-off Stelco workers are due back in Hamilton.

keyDates.label: Bank of Canada and Fed rate decisions
keyDates.why: Both central banks decide the same day; the Bank of Canada has said more hikes are possible.

keyDates.label: U.S. government funding deadline
keyDates.why: Federal funding runs out unless the outgoing Congress passes a spending bill or a temporary extension, which is also the likeliest vehicle for any new air traffic control money.

stories.headline: Canada could turn to Chinese automakers without US deal: Carney
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Monday that Canada could turn to Chinese automakers to shore up its struggling auto industry if trade negotiations with the Trump administration fail to produce a deal. Speaking to reporters in Cambodia, Carney said he remains focused on reaching an agreement with the U.S. but…

sources.title: The Hill: Canada could turn to Chinese automakers without US deal: Carney

stories.now: The Guardian: Ahead of Apec summit, PM says ‘Canada is going to move forward either way’ when asked if Chinese investment was leverage in US negotiations The prime minister of Canada, Mark Carney, said the country could turn to…
stories.backstory: The United States has imposed tariffs on Canadian steel, aluminum, vehicles and other goods since 2025, and Canada answered with counter-tariffs plus relief programs for its own importers. Washington announced further tariffs on Canadian goods in July, and Canada pulled out of negotiations in the summer after last-minute U.S. demands. The North American trade pact known as CUSMA in Canada and USMCA in the United States is also under review. After Democrats won Congress on Nov. 3, Carney said the Trump administration is still the side Canada has to negotiate with.
